set.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. It climbs a thin crack just right of Staudersaurus and Lickalotapuss.

review.notes: Corridor approach from the area pages; start position from the route Location line. No descent source for corridor routes.

set.approach: Lime-Aid is a northwest-facing formation to the south of Table Top Rock, a little to the southwest of Shark Fin. One way in is a straight climb on foot from the west end of Pioneer Lane; or by following the trail past The Gardens up the steep rocky hillside of the Upper Hill and splitting off to the formation. The route is on the right side of the west face.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: Drive up Keller Peak Road to Campsite 2. A trail starts near the campsite entrance and skirts it on the right; do not walk through the campsite when it is occupied. Little Pleasures Rock sits behind the campsite. The route climbs a right-facing lieback flake to a chimney on the east face, just left of Life's Little Pleasures.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: Use the approach that Morning Wall and Jedi Spire share: keep to the streambed and continue beyond the Jedi Spire turnoff. Lonesome Dove Rock is a big formation to the right of the stream; the east face has a distinctive recess at its centre, and the route climbs it.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: From the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead, hike up to Long Lake, a good spot to camp. The buttress shows through and above the trees to the northeast. The route starts around the corner left of Magic Staircase, on a clean white face cut by a hand crack, right below that route's second-pitch corner.
set.descent_text: The climbs on this buttress are gear-only and the descent is a walk-off.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: From the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead, hike up to Long Lake, a good spot to camp. The buttress shows through and above the trees to the northeast. Look for the prominent second-pitch corner about halfway up the face, to the left of the wall's highest section; the first pitch is blocky fourth class to easy fifth class up to its base.
set.descent_text: Build a gear belay at the top of the second pitch and walk off.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: From the north near Coyote Crag, hike west past Camp Rock to a clear, much-used path heading south into the trees; at the split keep left and continue southeast until the northwest corner of Lost Orbit Rock comes into view. From the southern parking area, head north beside the west side of Parkinglot Rock, then northeast on a faint trail to the south end of the formation. The route is the chimney behind the big tan flake, with Stand Up Comedy on the flake's left.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: Take forest road 2N13 east from Green Valley Lake. Low Maintenance Rock is the nearest formation visible beside the road on the left, and you park on the roadside. The route starts low on the left, beside Couple of Pitons Here on its right, and traverses diagonally right and up.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.
